LanguageData.TUBAD_ModName: This Used to Be About Dungeons
LanguageData.TUBAD_Finder_Open: Find dungeons by level, distance and party.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Finder_PartyHint: Hides dungeons any ticked pawn has entered. Untick retainers who won't go in.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Finder_LoadCaravan_Disabled: Select one of your caravans on the world map first.
LanguageData.TUBAD_EnterDungeon_Desc: Choose up to {0} people, plus any animals and mechs, and the items and supplies they take in. Each person can enter a given dungeon only once. Everyone not chosen waits here with the caravan.
LanguageData.TUBAD_CaravanMoving: The caravan must stop on this tile first.
LanguageData.TUBAD_EnterThingCountTip: How many to take into the dungeon.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Enter_People_Tip: People going in, out of at most {0}. Animals and mechs do not count.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Enter_Wealth_Tip: Market value of the pawns going in and what they wear and wield. Items carried in do not count. Raises the effective level.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Enter_AlreadyEntered: Already entered this dungeon, and cannot go in again: {0}.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Enter_EnteredTip: Has already entered this dungeon, and cannot go in again.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Enter_EnteredStuck: Already entered this dungeon, and cannot stay outside on their own: {0}. Leave a non-downed colonist outside with them.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Enter_LockedTip: Cannot stay outside on their own. Leave a non-downed colonist with them to allow them to stay outside.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Enter_Everyone: No caravan left outside. Only the items and supplies you select enter the dungeon; the rest wait at the entrance and are lost if the whole party dies.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Enter_NeedColonist: The party needs at least one colonist who is not downed.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Enter_TooMany: At most {0} people can enter a dungeon. Animals and mechs do not count.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Enter_TooManyEveryone: At most {0} people can enter a dungeon. Nobody would stay with the caravan, so everyone in it would go in: leave a colonist outside, or take fewer people.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Entered_Text: The party has entered a level {0} dungeon, generated at effective level {1} for them.\n\nTo leave, select the exit at the entrance and choose who leaves and what they carry out. If everyone in the party dies, the dungeon and anything left in it are gone.
LanguageData.TUBAD_LeaveDungeon_Desc: Choose who leaves and which items they carry out. They fetch the items, bring them here and rejoin the caravan outside.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Leave_NoPawns: Choose at least one pawn to leave.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Invite_Accepted: {PAWN_nameDef} agrees to leave with the party, and goes to wait by the entrance. Mark [PAWN_objective] in the leave dialog when the party goes.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Invite_Refused: {PAWN_nameDef} would rather stay in the dungeon.
LanguageData.TUBAD_ArrestHere: Arrest {0} where {1_pronoun} stands ({2} chance to accept)
LanguageData.TUBAD_Arrested: {PAWN_nameDef} is now your prisoner. Choose [PAWN_objective] in the leave dialog to take [PAWN_objective] out.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Dweller_Joined_Text: {PAWN_nameDef} came up out of the dungeon with the party and has decided to stay with you. [PAWN_pronoun] is now a member of your colony.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Dweller_Left: {PAWN_nameDef} came up out of the dungeon with the party, thanked them, and went [PAWN_possessive] own way.
LanguageData.TUBAD_PartyLost_Text: Nobody from the party made it out of the level {0} dungeon. The dungeon is closed, and everything inside it is gone.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_PartySize_Desc: Counts people only. Animals and mechs can go in on top of this.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_WealthToDouble_Desc: A dungeon is generated at its level times 1 + party wealth / this value. Party wealth is the pawns going in plus what they wear and wield. Example: a party worth {0} entering a level 10 dungeon meets effective level {1}.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_ShowIcons: Show dungeon icons on the world map
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_ShowIcons_Tip: Also toggled by the dungeon button with the other world map toggles in the bottom right.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_TintByLevel_Tip: Colours dungeon icons from green at level 1, through yellow and red, to purple at the maximum level.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_Generation_Desc: These settings apply when a world's dungeons are generated: new worlds, and existing saves that have never had dungeons. Worlds that already have dungeons keep them.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_Spacing_Desc: Minimum distance between two dungeons. Each step up roughly halves to thirds how many dungeons a world gets.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_Skew_Desc: At 1 every level is equally common; higher values make low levels more common. Now about {1} of dungeons are level {0} or lower, and {3} are level {2}.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_Roughness_Desc: Levels rise and fall across the world like terrain. Higher values give more, smaller peaks and valleys; lower values give a few broad regions.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_Ocean_Tip: When Vehicle Framework is active, dungeons are also placed on water tiles, reachable by boat.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_Creatures_Desc: Every creature in a dungeon is a titan. Each chamber may hold one pack, which wakes the first time any of the chamber is seen. These settings apply to dungeons entered from now on.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_Occupancy: Chance a chamber has a pack: {0}
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_EntranceChance: Chance the entrance chamber has a pack: {0}
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_MaxPackSize_Desc: Animals come in their species' usual group size, up to this. Insects come 2 to 4 at a time, mechanoids 1 to 3, people 1 to 4.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_MadChance_Desc: Animals and people only. Dungeon-mad creatures attack anything that is not also mad, never recover, and cannot be captured or tamed. The rest are wild animals that can be tamed and people who keep to their rooms. Insects and mechanoids are always hostile.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_StoneChance: Chance a pack is made of stone: {0}
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_StoneChance_Desc: Usually the dungeon's own rock, otherwise a random metal, stone or wood. Not mechanoids. The material comes on top of the pack's titan points.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_InviteChance: Chance a dweller agrees to leave: {0}
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_InviteChance_Desc: Multiplied by the inviting colonist's social impact. A dweller who refuses cannot be asked again, but can be arrested where they stand and taken out as a prisoner.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_JoinChance: Chance a dweller joins the colony: {0}
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_JoinChance_Desc: Rolled when a dweller comes out of the dungeon with the party. Otherwise they go their own way.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_PointsPerLevel_Desc: A pack's titan points average this times the effective level, and are split between its members, rounded up. All members share the same traits. Example: at effective level 10 a pack averages {0} points, so each wolf in a pack of 4 gets {1}.
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_PointNoise: Point variation: up to {0} either way
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_PowerBase: Strongest species at level 0: {0} combat power
LanguageData.TUBAD_Settings_Power_Desc: Species are random, but none stronger than this. Weak species can still turn up at any level, carrying more titan points. Now: up to {0} at level 1, {1} at level 10, {2} at level 30. A wolf is 75, a megaspider 150, a thrumbo 500.
